---
title: "Scenarios Zoo"
subtitle: "Workload Statistics, Scale Profiles, and Comparison Anchors"
---

The Scenarios Zoo holds reusable narrative and teaching anchors: real-world
workload statistics, energy and emissions comparison baselines, mobile power
envelopes, phone batteries, clinical-imaging workflow anchors, storage running
examples, and distributed-training scale profiles. These are not hardware specs
and not literature categories; provenance records where the number came from,
while the registry path records what kind of fact it is.

Use `Scenarios.*` for reusable problem settings that appear across examples. Use
`Hardware.*` for device specifications, `Systems.*` for composed physical systems
such as nodes/racks/clusters/storage paths, `Infrastructure.*` for facility,
pricing, grid, and capacity facts, and `Ops.*` for operational policies or
overhead profiles. A one-off hypothetical knob can stay local in a LEGO cell when
it defines the local problem rather than a shared fact.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
import mlsysim
from mlsysim.core.provenance import scalar_value

sections = [
    ("Workload scale anchors", mlsysim.Scenarios.Workloads),
    ("Clinical imaging anchors", mlsysim.Scenarios.ClinicalImaging),
    ("Energy comparison anchors", mlsysim.Scenarios.EnergyAnchors),
    ("Emissions comparison anchors", mlsysim.Scenarios.EmissionsAnchors),
    ("Training scale profiles", mlsysim.Scenarios.TrainingScaleProfiles),
    ("Storage training corpus", mlsysim.Scenarios.StorageTrainingCorpus),
    ("Mobile power envelopes", mlsysim.Scenarios.MobilePower),
    ("Phone battery anchors", mlsysim.Scenarios.PhoneBattery),
]

for title, reg in sections:
    print(f"## {title}\n")
    print("| Entry | Value | Description |")
    print("|:---|:---:|:---|")
    for item in reg.list():
        name = getattr(item, "name", type(item).__name__)
        desc = getattr(item, "description", "") or "---"
        if hasattr(item, "provenance"):
            try:
                val = scalar_value(item)
            except TypeError:
                val = f"{item:~P}"
        else:
            val = item
        print(f"| **{name}** | {val} | {desc} |")
    print()
```
